questions.stem: Microlaryngeal surgery is highly ____, so movement must be avoided.
questions.answer: stimulating

questions.stem: What special tube does laser microlaryngeal surgery need?
questions.answer: A laser tube

questions.stem: In jet ventilation for microlaryngeal surgery, where is the jet needle fixed?
questions.answer: To the proximal end of the suspension laryngoscope

questions.stem: A thin semi-rigid catheter, such as Hunsaker or Benjet, is passed through the ____ into the mid trachea.
questions.answer: glottis

questions.stem: In jet ventilation through the neck, through which membrane is the cannula placed?
During jet ventilation, which sign should be watched for?
questions.answer: Chest rise

questions.stem: In jet ventilation, why does the delivered FiO2 vary?
questions.answer: Entrainment

questions.stem: In microlaryngeal surgery, what decides the ventilation plan?
questions.answer: Site and nature of the lesion (glottic or subglottic)

questions.stem: What is the standard microlaryngeal tube size for non-laser anterior glottic surgery?
What does the abbreviation MLT stand for in microlaryngeal surgery?
questions.answer: Microlaryngeal tube

questions.stem: Which anaesthetic technique is used for tubeless microlaryngeal surgery?
Why is paralysis preferred in microlaryngeal surgery?
questions.answer: To stop vocal cord and patient movement

questions.stem: What does topical local anaesthetic do in microlaryngeal surgery?
questions.answer: Reduces stimulation

questions.stem: Which drug limits airway swelling after microlaryngeal surgery?
Why is glycopyrrolate given in microlaryngeal surgery?
questions.answer: As an antisialagogue to improve the surgical view

questions.stem: What should emergence from microlaryngeal surgery be like?
questions.answer: Smooth, avoiding bucking

questions.stem: What should be expected in patients returning for re-exploration after microlaryngeal surgery?
questions.answer: A difficult airway

questions.stem: What is microlaryngoscopy?
questions.answer: Examination of the larynx with an operating microscope

questions.stem: What are the diagnostic uses of microlaryngoscopy?
questions.answer: Assess laryngeal lesions, biopsy suspected pathology, investigate hoarseness

questions.stem: Which is a therapeutic use of microlaryngoscopy?
Which four tools can be used for endoscopic resection of laryngeal cancer?
questions.answer: Laser, cold steel, microdebrider or cautery

questions.stem: For microlaryngoscopy with retrognathia, where the larynx cannot be exposed, what should be considered?
options: Pushing harder on the jaw during laryngoscopy
Routine use of a larger tracheal tube

questions.stem: For microlaryngoscopy in elderly smokers, which systems need thorough assessment?
What patient position is used for microlaryngoscopy?
options: Lateral position, head turned away, head up
Supine, shoulder roll, head flexed and head up
Supine, shoulder roll, head extended and head down

questions.stem: Apart from a microlaryngoscopy tube, which airway approach can be used for microlaryngoscopy?
In microlaryngoscopy, how is anaesthesia of the cords achieved?
questions.answer: Topical local anaesthetic to the cords

questions.stem: For microlaryngoscopy, what duration of paralysis is advised?
In microlaryngoscopy, which drug is considered to reduce airway oedema?
In microlaryngoscopy, which drug is considered to reduce airway secretions?
Panendoscopy combines which kind of examination?
questions.answer: Endoscopic examination of the upper aerodigestive tract

questions.stem: Why would a tumour biopsy be done during panendoscopy?
questions.answer: Tumour not reachable under local anaesthesia in clinic

questions.stem: What is one purpose of panendoscopy in microlaryngeal surgery?
options: Reverse neuromuscular blockade at the end

questions.stem: In panendoscopy, is the full examination usually required for each patient?
questions.answer: No, most patients do not need every component

questions.stem: Panendoscopy is usually done under which anaesthetic, especially if bronchoscopy is needed?
Which airway is usually enough for panendoscopy?
Panendoscopy anaesthesia follows the approach of which other procedure?
questions.answer: Microlaryngoscopy

questions.stem: For panendoscopy, how should the table head be turned relative to the anaesthetist?
For panendoscopy, how far is the head of the bed raised?
Panendoscopy may combine biopsy with which other technique?
